title: Raising the Emotional and Narrative Stakes
use_cases: Implement when the protagonist's internal conflict needs to affect external characters
Use when developing higher stakes for communal or societal subplots
Configure when drafting relational drama involving fractured families or friendships
Use when establishing the psychological cost of a character's failure to change
content:
- Moral failure: When the protagonist’s inaction hurts others, not just themselves.
- Broader disaster: Communal or societal costs. Think innocent lives at risk or systems left unchanged in crime stories.
- Relational fallout: Damaged marriages, lost friendships, fractured families. This lands hard for drama or family stories.
- Personal loss: Loneliness, missed purpose, broken self-worth. If Cheryl quits the trail in “Wild,” her wounds go unhealed.

Double the tension by showing what your protagonist loses—and who else pays the price if they stay the same.
